title: Philemon Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Philemon chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Philemon Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Philemon Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Philemon 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Paul appears first as he is mentioned in the first verse of the chapter as 'Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ'.

questions.question: Who is mentioned as a fellow labourer with Philemon?
questions.explanation: Timothy is referred to as 'our brother' and a fellow labourer alongside Philemon in Philemon 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is the letter addressed?
questions.explanation: The letter is specifically addressed to Philemon as stated in Philemon 1:1.

questions.question: What does Paul thank God for in his prayers?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that he makes mention of Philemon always in his prayers, thanking God for Philemon's love and faith in Philemon 1:4-5.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Paul and Philemon as stated in verse 1?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to Philemon as 'our dearly beloved' in Philemon 1:1.

questions.question: Who does Paul mention alongside Philemon in his greetings?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions Apphia, Archippus, and the church in Philemon's house in Philemon 1:2.

questions.question: What does Paul desire for Philemon in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Paul wishes grace and peace to Philemon from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ in Philemon 1:3.

questions.question: What refreshes the bowels of the saints according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul states that they have great joy and consolation in Philemon's love because it refreshes the saints in Philemon 1:7.

questions.question: What does Paul hope the communication of Philemon's faith will become?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses hope that the communication of Philemon's faith may become effectual in Philemon 1:6.

questions.question: How does Paul refer to himself in verse 9?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to himself as 'Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ' in Philemon 1:9.

questions.question: Does Paul claim to be bold in Christ?
questions.explanation: Paul states that he might be much bold in Christ to enjoin Philemon, as mentioned in Philemon 1:8.

questions.question: Is Philemon mentioned as a fellow soldier?
questions.explanation: Archippus is mentioned as a fellow soldier in Philemon 1:2.

questions.question: Did Paul thank God for Philemon's love?
questions.explanation: Paul thanks God for Philemon's love and faith in Philemon 1:5.

questions.question: Paul writes this letter from a place of freedom.
questions.explanation: Paul identifies himself as a prisoner of Jesus Christ in Philemon 1:1, indicating he is not in a position of freedom.

questions.question: Timothy is mentioned as a fellow soldier.
questions.explanation: Timothy is referred to as a brother and not as a fellow soldier in the text; Archippus is the one called a fellow soldier in Philemon 1:2.

medium.title: Philemon Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Philemon Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: For whom does Paul beseech Philemon?
questions.explanation: Paul requests Philemon to receive Onesimus, whom he refers to as his son, in Philemon 1:10.

questions.question: What does Philemon 1:11 promise will happen if someone receives Onesimus as Paul requests in Philemon 1:10?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:11 states that Onesimus, who was previously unprofitable, is now profitable, indicating the gain of a brother through acceptance.

questions.question: What does Paul hope Onesimus will do for him in prison?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses his desire to retain Onesimus to minister to him while he is in bonds for the gospel, as stated in Philemon 1:13.

questions.question: What is Paul's reason for not keeping Onesimus with him?
options: He does not want to burden Philemon
He wants to test Philemon's faith
questions.explanation: In Philemon 1:14, Paul emphasizes that he did not want to act without Philemon's consent, highlighting the importance of willing actions.

questions.question: What might be a reason Onesimus left Philemon, according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul suggests that perhaps Onesimus departed for a season so that Philemon could receive him forever, implying a redemptive purpose in Philemon 1:15.

questions.question: How does Paul describe Onesimus' new status?
questions.explanation: In Philemon 1:16, Paul states that Onesimus is not just a servant but a beloved brother, highlighting the transformation in their relationship.

questions.question: What does Paul ask Philemon to do if he considers Paul a partner?
questions.explanation: Paul urges Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul himself, as stated in Philemon 1:17.

questions.question: What does Paul offer to take responsibility for?
questions.explanation: In Philemon 1:18, Paul offers to put any wrongs Onesimus has done on his own account, indicating his willingness to take responsibility.

questions.question: What is the nature of Paul's relationship with Onesimus?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to Onesimus as a beloved brother, indicating their relationship in Christ, as shown in Philemon 1:16.

questions.question: What does Philemon 1:7 reveal about Philemon's character?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:7 highlights that the bowels of the saints are refreshed by Philemon's love, indicating his encouraging and supportive nature.

questions.question: According to Philemon 1:6, what does Paul desire to be effective in Philemon's life?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses in Philemon 1:6 that he wants the communication of Philemon's faith to be effective through acknowledging the good things in him.

questions.question: What does Philemon 1:5 say Philemon has towards all saints?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:5 states that Philemon has love and faith towards the Lord Jesus and all saints, indicating his character.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul was bold to enjoin Philemon on matters of faith?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in Philemon 1:8 that he could be bold to enjoin Philemon but chooses to beseech him instead.

questions.question: Is it false that Paul wrote this letter while free and unchained?
questions.explanation: Paul identifies himself as a prisoner of Jesus Christ in Philemon 1:1, indicating he was indeed imprisoned while writing.

questions.question: Is it false that Paul had no personal relationship with Onesimus?
questions.explanation: Paul refers to Onesimus as his son, indicating a personal relationship with him, as noted in Philemon 1:10.

hard.title: Philemon Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Philemon Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Philemon 1:19, what does Paul promise to do with his own hand?
options: I will write a second letter
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:19 states, 'I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it', indicating Paul's personal commitment to repay the debt.

questions.question: According to Philemon 1:20, what does Paul desire from Philemon in the Lord?
options: Let me have joy of thee
questions.correctAnswer: Let me have joy of thee
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:20 says, 'Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord', showing Paul's desire for joy through Philemon's actions.

questions.question: What confidence does Paul express in Philemon 1:21 regarding Philemon's response?
options: Philemon will do more than Paul says
questions.correctAnswer: Philemon will do more than Paul says
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:21 states, 'Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say', expressing Paul's trust in Philemon's generous response.

questions.question: In Philemon 1:22, what does Paul ask Philemon to prepare?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:22 says, 'But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you', indicating Paul's request for a place to stay.

questions.question: Who is identified as Paul's fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus in Philemon 1:23?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:23 identifies Epaphras as 'my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus', showing his shared imprisonment with Paul.

questions.question: Which group of men are named as Paul's fellow laborers in Philemon 1:24?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:24 lists these four men as Paul's 'fellowlabourers', showing their ministry partnership.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'καρδία' (kardia) in Philemon 1:7 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'καρδία' (kardia) means 'heart', referring to the seat of affection or love, which aligns with the context of Philemon 1:7 about love and consolation.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Philemon 1:16 where Onesimus is called 'not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved'?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:16 uses contrast by setting 'servant' against 'brother beloved', highlighting the changed relationship, which is a clear example of antithesis.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of forgiveness and restoration found in Philemon 1:18 where Paul says 'put that on mine account'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:4-6 speaks of the suffering servant bearing others' iniquities, which parallels Paul's willingness to take Onesimus' debt upon himself in Philemon 1:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of brotherly love and reconciliation emphasized in Philemon 1:16?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:10 exhorts believers to 'be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love', directly reflecting the brotherly relationship Paul urges in Philemon 1:16.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul's request in Philemon 1:22 to prepare a lodging for him?
options: Paul expresses confidence that Philemon will do even more than he asks
Paul asks Philemon to forgive Onesimus
Paul sends greetings from fellow workers
Paul thanks God for Philemon's love
questions.correctAnswer: Paul expresses confidence that Philemon will do even more than he asks
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:21 precedes verse 22 and says, 'Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say', immediately before the lodging request.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of Onesimus in the context of Philemon 1:10-16?
options: He represents the transformed believer, moving from slavery to brotherhood
He is a symbol of the Old Testament law
He illustrates the rejection of the gospel
He typifies the Roman governmental authority
questions.correctAnswer: He represents the transformed believer, moving from slavery to brotherhood
questions.explanation: Onesimus' journey from unprofitable servant to beloved brother in Philemon 1:10-16 typologically symbolizes conversion and reconciliation in Christ.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'refreshing of the bowels' in Philemon 1:20 relate to ancient Greek cultural understanding?
options: It metaphorically expresses deep emotional comfort and affection
It refers to a physical healing ritual
questions.correctAnswer: It metaphorically expresses deep emotional comfort and affection
questions.explanation: In Greek culture, 'bowels' often symbolized the seat of emotions and compassion; thus, 'refresh my bowels' in Philemon 1:20 is a metaphor for emotional refreshment and joy.

questions.question: True or False: Paul explicitly commands Philemon to receive Onesimus back as a servant in Philemon 1:14.
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:14 states, 'But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly', showing Paul does not command but requests willingly.

questions.question: True or False: Paul acknowledges in Philemon 1:19 that Philemon owes him even his own self besides the debt to Onesimus.
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:19 says, 'albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides', indicating Paul affirms a spiritual debt from Philemon to himself.

theological.title: Philemon Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Philemon Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Philemon 1:6 teach about sanctification?
options: Faith must be expressed through acknowledging the good in Christ to become effective
Sanctification is solely an inward experience without external expression
Grace alone without faith produces sanctification
Sanctification is attained by works apart from faith
questions.correctAnswer: Faith must be expressed through acknowledging the good in Christ to become effective
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:6 states that the communication of faith becomes effectual by acknowledging every good thing in Christ, emphasizing the role of faith's expression in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian fellowship does Philemon 1:7 emphasize?
options: The love among saints refreshes and consoles believers
Fellowship is primarily a social gathering without spiritual significance
Christian fellowship is optional for spiritual growth
Love is not necessary for true fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: The love among saints refreshes and consoles believers
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:7 highlights joy and consolation in love because 'the bowels of the saints are refreshed' by the brother’s love, emphasizing fellowship's spiritual refreshment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning Christian reconciliation is taught in Philemon 1:16?
options: A former servant is to be received not as a servant but as a beloved brother in Christ
Reconciliation is impossible between masters and servants
Only social equality matters, not spiritual
Christians should maintain social distinctions even after conversion
questions.correctAnswer: A former servant is to be received not as a servant but as a beloved brother in Christ
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:16 instructs that Onesimus is to be received not as a servant but as a beloved brother, showing the transformative power of reconciliation in Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Philemon 1:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:3 opens with a greeting of grace and peace from God and the Lord Jesus Christ, demonstrating God's attribute of grace.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in Philemon 1:9?
questions.explanation: Paul’s gentle appeal 'for love’s sake' in Philemon 1:9 demonstrates longsuffering, showing patience and kindness in persuasion rather than command.

questions.question: How does Philemon 1:10-12 connect with the broader biblical theme of redemption?
options: It illustrates the transformation and restoration of a formerly unprofitable servant into a beloved brother
It teaches that social status cannot change even after conversion
It denies the possibility of forgiveness for those who have sinned
It emphasizes strict legalism over grace
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the transformation and restoration of a formerly unprofitable servant into a beloved brother
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:10-12 shows Onesimus, once unprofitable, now profitable and sent back as a beloved brother, paralleling biblical themes of redemption and restoration.

questions.question: In what way does Philemon 1:15-16 connect with the theme of new identity in Christ as found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It teaches that believers receive a new eternal identity beyond former social roles
It insists believers remain in their previous worldly identities
It denies spiritual rebirth and transformation
It focuses only on earthly reconciliation without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that believers receive a new eternal identity beyond former social roles
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:15-16 shows Onesimus’s departure was for a season so he could be received forever 'not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved', demonstrating the new identity in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Philemon 1:8 and 1:9 teach about Christian persuasion and authority?
options: Authority in Christ is exercised with love and voluntary submission, not compulsion
Authority must always be imposed regardless of love
Christian persuasion is irrelevant in the exercise of authority
Love is less important than legal command
questions.correctAnswer: Authority in Christ is exercised with love and voluntary submission, not compulsion
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:8 shows Paul could enjoin what is convenient, but 1:9 reveals he beseeches for love’s sake, teaching authority is most effective when exercised in love and voluntary submission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Philemon 1:17 and 1:18 teach about Christian responsibility and restitution?
options: Christian fellowship includes accepting others as oneself and bearing each other’s debts
Each believer is responsible only for themselves
questions.correctAnswer: Christian fellowship includes accepting others as oneself and bearing each other’s debts
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:17 urges reception of Onesimus 'as myself' and 1:18 offers Paul’s willingness to repay any wrong, indicating mutual responsibility and restitution within Christian fellowship.

questions.question: What combined truth about prayer and Christian community does Philemon 1:4 and 1:22 teach?
options: Prayer for others is vital and linked to hope for mutual fellowship
Prayer is only for private benefit, not community
Prayer is not connected to Christian hospitality
Prayer is unnecessary when physical presence is possible
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer for others is vital and linked to hope for mutual fellowship
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:4 mentions constant prayer for Philemon, and 1:22 Paul expresses hope to visit, showing prayer’s vital role in sustaining and anticipating Christian fellowship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Philemon 1:10-19 condones slavery by urging Onesimus’s return to his master. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches the transformation of social relationships through Christian love and brotherhood
It endorses the permanence of slavery without change
It ignores the plight of Onesimus entirely
It promotes social hierarchy as unchangeable
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the transformation of social relationships through Christian love and brotherhood
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:10-19 shows Paul appealing for Onesimus to be received 'not as a servant but as a brother,' emphasizing Christian transformation of social roles rather than endorsement of slavery.

questions.question: What doctrine does Philemon 1:25 teach about the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ?
options: Grace is the sustaining presence with the believer’s spirit
Grace is only an external blessing without internal effect
Grace is limited to certain spiritual gifts
Grace is unrelated to the believer’s inner life
questions.correctAnswer: Grace is the sustaining presence with the believer’s spirit
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:25 closes with a blessing of grace being with the spirit, indicating grace sustains and indwells the believer internally.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Philemon 1:19 by Paul's personal guarantee?
questions.explanation: Paul’s personal written promise to repay any debt in Philemon 1:19 demonstrates God’s attribute of faithfulness mirrored in apostolic responsibility.

questions.question: How does Philemon 1:23–24 contribute to the narrative arc of apostolic ministry in the early church?
options: It shows the communal support and partnership among early Christian workers
It denies the involvement of others in ministry
It focuses only on Paul without mention of others
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the communal support and partnership among early Christian workers
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:23-24 lists fellow prisoners and laborers, highlighting the interconnected community and teamwork in early apostolic ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Christian love and obedience does Philemon 1:5 and 1:21 teach?
options: Love and faith toward the Lord and saints leads to joyful obedience beyond command
Faithfulness does not affect Christian conduct
Obedience is compelled by fear rather than love
questions.correctAnswer: Love and faith toward the Lord and saints leads to joyful obedience beyond command
questions.explanation: Philemon 1:5 mentions love and faith toward Jesus and saints, and 1:21 expresses confidence Philemon will do more than commanded, showing love’s role in joyful obedience.
